text:
maya_sales: Hey team — AcmeHealth wants a Dedicated pool POC but their security team insists on static outbound IPs for allowlisting and an explanation of IP rotation policy. Also asking for a quote for POC setup (1 month). Can ops/eng confirm options?
jordan_eng: We have two viable approaches: managed egress (we present a stable outbound IP block for the pool) or customer-managed egress (VPC peering / Private deployment + customer NAT). For a short POC managed egress is fastest.
neha_secu: From the questionnaire: they need a CIDR (or list of /32s), a diagram showing network flow, and what triggers IP changes. They also asked about port restrictions and TLS termination requirements.
alex_ops: Quick summary on constraints: managed-egress = Redwood maintains NAT + we provide static IPs tied to the Dedicated pool. Rotation only happens during maintenance or failover events; we provide 48h notice for planned changes. customer-egress = customer manages egress so IPs are fully in their control. Managed-egress has a small setup fee + monthly allocation cost.
maya_sales: Cool. Two asks for the customer: 1) sample allowlist entries we can hand them, 2) a ballpark number for setup/month for a 1-month POC.
jordan_eng: Sample allowlist lines (copy these into their firewall):
```
# allowlist for Redwood Dedicated POC
203.0.113.45/32  # primary outbound NAT for pool A
203.0.113.46/32  # failover NAT (only used on failover)
```
Also include destination ports: 443 (HTTPS) outbound to our API endpoints (api.redwood.ai and *.redwood-internal.svc). If they want to lock by FQDN and TLS SNI that's fine but many firewalls prefer IPs.
neha_secu: For the questionnaire text we should add this wording: "Outbound IPs are assigned to the Dedicated pool. Redwood will provide the current list of /32 IP addresses and will notify the customer 48 hours prior to any planned change. Unplanned changes (rare—e.g., due to emergency maintenance) will be communicated via the designated incident channel and postmortem." Use that in the SQA response.
alex_ops: Pricing for short POC (estimate): setup fee = $2,000 (one-time) to allocate static NAT and document network runbook; monthly = $350 for the NAT allocation + $0.15 per 1k tokens (standard Dedicated rate applies). If they convert to reserved capacity contract we roll setup into the contract.
maya_sales: Perfect. Can we also provide a tiny network diagram snippet to paste into their SQA?
jordan_eng: ASCII diagram below — keep it minimal for the questionnaire:
```
Customer VPC
  |---> Firewall (allowlist: 203.0.113.45/32:443)
  |---> Internet --> Redwood Managed NAT (203.0.113.45)
  |---> Redwood Dedicated Pool --> API endpoint
```
maya_sales: Nice. Two final asks from customer: "What happens if the IP changes unexpectedly?" and "Are temporary IPs during pool autoscaling possible?"
jordan_eng: Unexpected change workflow: we send incident notification -> provide fallback IPs if available -> apply routing fix. It's rare. Autoscaling of Dedicated nodes doesn't change NAT IPs for the pool; we avoid IP churn by keeping NAT stable for the pool. Temporary extra egress addresses can be provisioned but are billed as additional NAT allocations and aren't guaranteed to be static long-term.
neha_secu: Also remind them to include a maintenance window clause — we give them at least 48h for planned maintenance that affects egress.
maya_sales: I'll send this back to AcmeHealth. Can someone create a concise SOW paragraph I can paste?
alex_ops: Putting a quick SOW blurb here you can copy: "Redwood will provision a Dedicated inference pool for AcmeHealth with managed egress. Redwood will allocate static outbound IPv4 addresses for allowlisting, provide a network runbook and notify AcmeHealth 48 hours prior to any planned egress IP changes. One-time setup fee $2,000 and $350/month for NAT allocation for the duration of the POC. Standard per-token Dedicated usage applies."
maya_sales: Perfect — copying into email now. thanks! :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Ticket #D-1987 created for NAT allocation request (owner: alex_ops).
maya_sales: tagging @neha_secu — I'll attach the network diagram and your SQA wording to the questionnaire response.
neha_secu: great, I'll review before send.
